Its panels: why now (loneliness), the two deaths of community (secular and spiritual), the escuelita mission (come in, live in, learn to hold, go out and start the next one), what’s missing (inner work and healthy structure), and six core design principles.

0b760a8e.alt: Infographic, “Building Healing Community – How It Could Work: a lived village, a training ground, and a path toward deeper common life”. Its panels: my journey, daily life in a healing community, why children need community, the couple problem, a path toward less money, shared inner purpose, practices that keep community alive, and the invitation.

7daf9ea4.alt: Diagram, “The Math of Absorption”: a community can absorb only as much need as its members have free resource to meet. With 8 people and 2 in crisis (1 in 4), everything goes to triage; with 80 people and 5 in crisis (1 in 16), they’re carried and barely felt. Small communities need new members most and can absorb them least.

8957e830.alt: Diagram of a house. The roof is Community. Three pillars hold it up: inner pl/ork (reparenting, somatic regulation, contemplative practice), relational pl/ork (peer counseling, jealousy processing, honesty practices, conflict handling) and medicine pl/ork (peer-guided, no shamans, gated behind the other work). They stand on the container: membership, land, money, governance, children and exit. If one of the four gets skipped, it will need to be dealt with eventually, at high stress.
